resolutions.rationale: Pine's creative-will qualification at 93:40-95:50 expressly acknowledges difficulty explaining creation or noncreation without real divine distinction. His precontained-differences reply at 110:55-113:13 also opens by questioning whether it directly addresses Schmid's objection. Option-b more precisely locates that latter limitation in responsiveness and includes the simplicity-of-being burden. These are identifiable move-level limitations, not an independent debate-wide consequence warranting a second deduction under the rubric's penalty controls.

Schmid's necessary-propositions argument at 30:38-32:47 explicitly moves from necessary truth to the existence of distinct truth-bearers; his internal-actualizer reply at 80:19-82:31 offers distinct aspects within God to answer the causal-circle concern. Option-b names both moves and the con-ideas burden, making its account of the remaining premises and alternative-model challenge more traceable than option-a's list. Neither passage creates a completion consequence separate from the individual arguments, and Schmid's critical role does not require establishing atheism or a complete rival theology.
